report_claims.alexandroupolis_plume: A fire in the country’s northeast near Alexandroupolis produced a plume of smoke that stretched hundreds of miles southwest toward Italy. The plume is visible in this image, acquired in the afternoon on August 22, 2023, by theVisible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) on the NOAA-NASA Suomi NPP satellite.
report_claims.annual_burned_area_context: area burned in Greece so far in 2023 has surpassed that of the destructive 2021 fire season
report_claims.athens_local_impact: Smaller plumes are visible from other fires burning elsewhere across the nation. According to news reports, fires near Athens burned homes and cars, and sent smoke wafting over the capital city.
report_claims.fire_weather_aug23: Forecasts called for extreme fire weather—hot, dry, and windy—to continue on August 23. By that day, smoke was detected over Italy and across the Mediterranean Sea in northern Africa.
report_claims.late_august_fires: A month after fires tore across parts of Greece in July 2023, dozens more fires ignited within 24 hours across the country in late August 2023.
report_claims.mediterranean_smoke: Forecasts called for extreme fire weather—hot, dry, and windy—to continue on August 23. By that day, smoke was detected over Italy and across the Mediterranean Sea in northern Africa.
